core_meaning.short_meaning: Resolute mover, swift walker; early steadfast companion Khabbab ibn al-Aratt.
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Khabbab (خَبَّاب) is an Arabic masculine given name meaning 'one who strides swiftly and resolutely' or 'energetic, steadfast champion'. In Islamic history, it is the illustrious name of Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, the sixth person to embrace Islam and one of the most steadfast early martyrs to endure torture for the Oneness of God.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: Intensive form of khabba (to trot, stride swiftly and purposefully), indicating agility, vitality, and steady forward progress.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The root kh-b-b in classical lexicons denotes a brisk, spirited gait. Khabbab ibn al-Aratt was among the very earliest converts in Mecca who faced extreme persecution by Quraysh, being laid on burning embers. He remained unshakeable in his faith, taught the Quran to the early Muslims, fought at Badr and Uhud, and was deeply honored by all the Caliphs.
